question: Explain the meaning of zero-rated supply under the IGST Act, 2017 and the options available to a supplier for claiming refund in respect of such supplies.

points.label: Meaning of zero-rated supply
points.description: Export of goods or services or both, and supply of goods or services or both for authorised operations to a Special Economic Zone developer or unit.

points.label: Input tax credit allowed
points.description: Input tax credit may be taken for making zero-rated supplies even if the supply is exempt, subject to the blocked credit provisions.

points.label: Supply under bond or LUT
points.description: The supplier may make the supply under a bond or letter of undertaking without paying integrated tax and claim refund of unutilised input tax credit.
points.basis: IGST Act, 2017, section 16(3); CGST Rules, 2017, rule 89

points.label: Supply on payment of integrated tax
points.description: Alternatively, the supplier may pay integrated tax and claim refund of the tax paid; after the 2023 amendment this route is available only to notified classes of persons or supplies. For exported goods, the shipping bill is treated as the refund application once the export details and a valid return are filed.
points.basis: IGST Act, 2017, section 16 as amended by the Finance Act, 2023 (refund on payment of integrated tax limited to notified classes); CGST Rules, 2017, rule 96

points.label: Time limit and provisional refund
points.description: A refund application must be made within two years from the relevant date; for zero-rated supplies the proper officer may grant a provisional refund of 90% of the amount claimed, pending final verification.
